details:
What We Developed & How It Works
Astrovia is an interactive 3D web platform designed to identify the closest Earth analogs for lunar and Martian landing sites before astronauts leave the planet. Users begin their journey in a dynamic cosmic environment featuring realistic, rotating 3D models of the Moon, Mars, and Earth (mapped with accurate continental geography).

By clicking on the Moon or Mars, users explore glowing markers representing real NASA landing zones (such as Shackleton Crater or Jezero Crater). Selecting a site displays its mission history alongside eight standardized NASA parameters: temperature, soil type, rock composition, slope, surface roughness, humidity, lighting, and gravity. Users then transition to the 3D Earth globe to evaluate terrestrial training sites. Clicking any Earth location triggers our custom matching algorithm—calculating individual trait similarity scores using the formula \(100 - (\text{Difference} \div \text{Max Possible Difference} \times 100)\) as well as an overall match percentage. Because no single place on Earth replicates off-world conditions 100%, clicking "Complete Missing Traits" prompts Astrovia to scan the database and pair complementary Earth locations that cover the missing parameters, achieving a combined 100% training match.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Astrovia addresses a critical gap in space mission preparation. By pinpointing exact geological and environmental matches upfront, the platform saves space agencies billions of dollars and valuable time by preventing costly hardware failures in inaccurate testing environments. Furthermore, it maximizes astronaut and rover readiness by ensuring crews train on the exact soil friction, slope angles, and lighting conditions they will encounter off-world. Ultimately, Astrovia aims to accelerate safe human expansion into the solar system—supporting upcoming missions like NASA’s Artemis program and future Mars exploration—while making complex planetary analog data accessible to researchers, engineers, and students worldwide.

Tools, Technologies & Data Sources

  • Frontend & 3D Graphics: Built using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), and Three.js / WebGL to render realistic 3D spheres, high-resolution NASA planetary textures, orbital animations, and interactive lighting.
  • Data Processing: Structured, normalized, and converted planetary datasets from Microsoft Excel into JSON format using Python (Pandas) to power the real-time comparison algorithm.
  • Scientific Data: Sourced from the NASA Open Data Portal, Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), and USGS terrestrial analog databases.
  • Design & Hardware: Designed in Figma, presented via Prezi, and developed on standard laptops optimized for WebGL rendering.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered
What makes Astrovia uniquely creative is its "puzzle-piece" pairing concept. Rather than acting as a static directory of analog sites, it actively solves single-site limitations by combining two or more terrestrial locations to reach 100% environmental coverage—wrapped in an intuitive, gamified 3D space interface. Throughout development, our team prioritized scientific accuracy (anchoring comparisons to eight measurable engineering criteria), geographical realism (accurately mapping real continents and coordinates such as Wadi Al-Hitan in Egypt, Atacama Desert in Chile, and Kilauea in Hawaii), intuitive UX/UI for effortless navigation, and web performance optimization so high-resolution 3D globes run smoothly across standard browsers.
